name: Storage

hero.title: A signal that remembers. In every tab, after every reload.
hero.lede: `useStorage('theme', 'light')` is a signal backed by localStorage: read it with `theme()`, write it with `theme.set()`, and every open tab follows. Session storage, cookies (readable during SSR), IndexedDB and custom backends work the same way, with versioned migrations built in.

items.title: It is a signal
items.text: `theme()` reads, `theme.set()` writes, `theme.remove()` deletes and returns to the default. Every component calling `useStorage('theme', …)` gets the same signal, and every tab updates through the `storage` event.

items.title: Old data upgrades itself
items.text: Give `version: 2` and a `migrate(old, from)`. A value written by last month's release, or by a tab still running it, is migrated on read. Values from before versioning arrive as `from = 0`.

items.title: The right theme on the first paint
items.text: `useCookie` reads the request's `Cookie` header during SSR. Under `renderToString` each request gets its own cookie signals, so concurrent users never see each other's values.

items.title: Failures don't crash the page
items.text: A corrupt stored value falls back to the default, private mode degrades to memory, and a quota error reaches `onError` while the UI keeps the new value.

before.label: localStorage by hand
before.caption: Parse, guard, listen, re-render, and remember the quota. Per key.

after.label: with @pyreon/storage
after.caption: A signal that is persisted, shared and synced.
after.code:
import { useStorage } from '@pyreon/storage'

const theme = useStorage<'light' | 'dark'>('theme', 'light')

theme() // 'light', or whatever was saved; a corrupt value falls back to the default
theme.set('dark') // saved, and every open tab updates
theme.remove() // back to 'light', entry deleted

features.title: Every place a browser can keep data.

items.text: large values; the signal updates at once and the write is debounced and flushed on `pagehide`.

items.text: your own backend, for example encrypted at rest.

api.title: Five hooks, a factory, two helpers.

limits.title: Not for secrets
limits.text: Browser storage is readable by any script on the page. On a device, use `useSecureStorage` from `@pyreon/hooks` for tokens.

limits.title: IndexedDB starts at the default
limits.text: Reads are async, so the signal shows the default until the stored value arrives.

limits.title: Concurrent SSR needs an accessor
limits.text: Pass `setCookieSource` a function that reads the current request, and render inside `renderToString` or `runWithRequestContext`, which isolate the cached signals per request. A plain string is one shared slot.

limits.title: One key, one set of options
limits.text: Every call for a key shares one signal, so a second call's different default is ignored, with a development warning.

benchmarks.rival: vs Jotai atomWithStorage and Zustand persist · bun / JavaScriptCore
benchmarks.p: All three libraries write to the same in-memory storage engine, and a correctness gate checks that all three agree before anything is timed. Reads are single-digit nanoseconds everywhere; Zustand's is one nanosecond quicker.

comingFrom.title: Persistence without a middleware or a store.
comingFrom.note: `name` becomes the key, `version` and `migrate` carry over, and cross-tab sync needs no listener. To persist part of a `@pyreon/store` store, return a `useStorage` signal from its setup instead of using `partialize`.

comingFrom.title: The atom is the signal.
comingFrom.note: No `useAtom` pair: read `theme()` anywhere and only that text updates. Other tabs follow through the `storage` event.

recipes.title: A theme with no flash, on a busy server
recipes.text: The cookie decides the server render, localStorage keeps other tabs in step, and concurrent requests each read their own cookie.

recipes.title: Reshape stored data without losing it
recipes.text: Users who stored `{ theme }` last month get `{ theme, density }` today, on first read.

faq.q: Does it really sync between tabs?
faq.a: Yes, through the browser's `storage` event, for localStorage-backed signals. A versioned value written by another tab is migrated before it lands. Session storage is per tab by definition.

faq.q: What happens in private mode or when storage is full?
faq.a: `useStorage` probes for write access and degrades to an in-memory value instead of throwing. A failed write calls `onError`; the signal keeps the new value so the UI stays consistent.
One overnight run under bun, against Jotai `atomWithStorage` and Zustand `persist` writing to the same in-memory engine. We wrote it; run `bun run --filter '@pyreon/storage' bench:storage`.
